findings.summary: `int writesBefore = 0` survives the whole 493-case suite INCLUDING the 1,000-seed sweep, and with it applied the M5.29 defect this commit exists to catch passes GREEN -- MEASURED both ways
findings.detail: Mutation: replace `int writesBefore = faulty.calls("putIfMatch");` with `int writesBefore = 0;`. Result: `./gradlew :sequencer:test` -> 493 testcases, 0 failures. The credit then means 'the release completed AND this store has EVER seen a putIfMatch', not 'this WINDOW issued one'. That is not theoretical: the compound measurement is decisive. Control, on the clean tree, with `leases.release()` at LocalSequencer.java:576 swapped for `store.stat(leases.key())` -- CommitProtocolSweepTest#theInvariantsHoldAcrossEverySeed REDS on the gracefulReleases floor, exactly as the commit body claims. Same production swap PLUS `writesBefore = 0` -- the sweep passes, 0 failures. So one edit to a test-helper line silently restores the pre-M5.29 blindness with nothing red, because lease acquire/renew already put a `putIfMatch` on that store before any release window. Nothing in the tree can see it: every case in GracefulReleaseMeterTest uses a fresh store and a SINGLE `observe`, so `writesBefore` is always 0 on a correct tree too. Kill (three lines, no new seam): one `observe` doing the putIfMatch, then a SECOND `observe` on the SAME store+meter with an empty lambda, asserting `released()` is 1 -- it is 2 under the mutation. Graded minor rather than major on this file's own precedent (M5.28's cell: 'the exposure is a future edit rather than today's coverage, and review.md rule 12 does not buy a round for that') and because the line it replaces, `int callsBefore = faulty.calls()`, carried the identical hole before this commit -- it is residual, not introduced. The natural home is M5.35, which already owns the two siblings `int before = 0` and `refusalsSeen = 0` at the top of the same `observe`; note this one is strictly worse than those, because the sweep catches `before = 0` and catches NOTHING here.
findings.failure_scenario: A later hand edits GracefulReleaseMeter.observe -- hoisting the baseline, or writing `int writesBefore = 0` while simplifying -- and every test stays green. The meter then credits any completed release on a store that has ever seen a putIfMatch, which every run has by lease acquire time. MEASURED: with that one line changed AND `leases.release()` at LocalSequencer.java:576 replaced by `store.stat(leases.key())`, CommitProtocolSweepTest passes green -- the same production defect reds the floor on the unmutated tree. The commit's headline evidence is then false with nothing red.

findings.summary: Round-2's minor is fixed for `stat` and NOT for `putIfMatch`: `record("putIfMatch")` moved below `refuseIfPartitioned()` still survives the full suite, so `calls(String)`'s 'refused ones included' is unpinned on the one verb the meter credits
findings.detail: Re-measured this round. `record("stat")` below `refuseIfPartitioned()` now DIES on the new assertion at GracefulReleaseMeterTest.java:107 (theLEADERSOWNPartitionIsSEENButBlamedOnNOBODYElse, expected 1 but was 0) -- that half of the round-2 minor is closed. The other half is not: moving `record("putIfMatch")` from FaultInjectingStore.java:596 to just BELOW the `refuseIfPartitioned()` at FaultInjectingStore.java:624 leaves 493 testcases green, sweep included. FaultInjectingStore.java:150 states 'Calls of ONE verb, refused ones included', and that claim is now constrained for `stat` (partition refusal) and for `list` (injected throw above the partition check, GracefulReleaseMeterTest.java:140) but not for the verb `GracefulReleaseMeter` actually credits. Live loss today is nil -- a refused putIfMatch throws, so `completed` is false and the credit cannot move either way -- which is why this is minor and was minor in round 2. Kill: in theLEADERSOWNPartitionIsSEENButBlamedOnNOBODYElse (or a sibling), have the partitioned leader attempt a `putIfMatch` and assert `faulty.calls("putIfMatch")` is 1.
findings.failure_scenario: Someone reorders putIfMatch so `record` sits below `refuseIfPartitioned()` -- e.g. while moving the partition guard or de-duplicating the verbs -- and the suite stays green at 493 testcases. `calls("putIfMatch")` then silently stops counting refused lease writes, contradicting calls(String)'s own javadoc, and any later assertion or sweep floor built on 'refused ones included' for the credited verb reasons from a number that is missing the refusals.
